Your profile starts with a few numbers
Log boulders on the board or a climbing day, and add a starting value for max hangs or weighted pull-ups. Then you will see where you stand and how grade and strength move together.

Grade and finger strength over time
As soon as there are board sends and finger values, both lines appear here week by week.
Working grade over %1$d weeks and %2$d finger strength values on a shared time axis.
%1$d more weeks with both a grade and a finger value, then we show how closely the two move together (now %2$d).
Strongly linked: in your data, weeks with stronger fingers are clearly weeks with a higher working grade.
Clearly linked: grade and finger strength usually rise together for you.
Weakly linked: other things move your grade at least as much as finger strength.
Hardly linked so far: your grade moves largely independently of finger strength.
Opposite so far: in weeks with more finger strength your grade was lower – often fatigue from a strength block.
A correlation shows moving together, not cause and effect.

The typical ranges are a rough orientation built from published climbing research and coaching surveys. People differ a lot – it is neither a goal nor a ranking, and nothing here suggests a body weight.
